Um … zu: a finalidade, passo a passo: Um … zu: purpose, step by step
PASSO 1: para dizer PARA QUÊ se faz algo: STEP 1: to say WHAT something is done FOR, use «UM … ZU» + infinitive — English "(in order) to": «Ich lerne Deutsch, um in Berlin zu arbeiten» (I'm learning German in order to work in Berlin). STEP 2: «um» opens the phrase; «zu» goes RIGHT BEFORE the infinitive at the end; with a separable verb: «um aufzustehen». STEP 3: RULE: the SUBJECT is the SAME in the main clause and in the «um … zu» phrase (here, «ich» does both things). STEP 4: a comma before «um». STEP 5: «um … zu» answers «Wozu?» (what for?) or «Warum?». STEP 6: don't use «um … zu» when the subject changes: then use «damit» (next session). Also: never translate "for" + -ing with «für» («für arbeiten» is wrong) — it's «um … zu arbeiten».

PASSO 1: «DAMIT» (para que) abre uma sub: STEP 1: «DAMIT» (so that) opens a subordinate clause of purpose. The conjugated verb goes to the END. STEP 2: use it when the subject of the main clause and that of the subordinate clause are DIFFERENT: «Ich erkläre es dir, damit du es verstehst» (I'm explaining it to you so that you understand it). STEP 3: you can also use it with the SAME subject, but «um … zu» is more common and shorter. STEP 4: «damit» isn't «mit» (with); it's one word, a conjunction. STEP 5: the comma before «damit» is required. STEP 6: question «Wozu?» (what for?); answer with «um … zu» or «damit».

PASSO 1: «OHNE … ZU» + infinitivo signif: STEP 1: «OHNE … ZU» + infinitive means "WITHOUT doing": «Er ging, ohne ein Wort zu sagen» (he left without saying a word). English uses -ing here; German uses «zu» + infinitive. STEP 2: «(AN)STATT … ZU» + infinitive means "INSTEAD OF doing": «Statt zu lernen, schaut er fern» (instead of studying, he watches TV). STEP 3: the subject is usually the same. STEP 4: with different subjects: «ohne dass» and «anstatt dass» + verb at the end: «Er ging, ohne dass jemand es merkte» (he left without anyone noticing). STEP 5: with a separable verb, «zu» goes in the middle: «statt fernzusehen», «ohne aufzustehen».
